images.caption: The remnants of the mansion built by Henry Middleton in the 1700's, near Charleston, South Carolina, in the southeastern United States. The main house and north flanker were burned during the U.S. Civil War, leaving only the south wing seen here. The house is now a national historic landmark and museum.
images.alt: The remnants of the mansion built by Henry Middleton in the 1700's, near Charleston, South Carolina, in the southeastern United States. images.caption: The Pink House, built circa 1712, in Charleston, South Carolina, USA. The house is listed on the National Register of Historic Places as a contributing building in the French Quarter District. As was by then typical of the Architecture of Bermuda, the house was built of limestone from Bermuda (Charleston had been settled from Bermuda under William Sayle in the 1670s, and Bermudians retained close links with the city up to American independence).
images.alt: The Pink House, built circa 1712, in Charleston, South Carolina, USA. The house is listed on the National Register of Historic Places as a contributing building in the French Quarter District. As was by then typical of the Architecture of Bermuda, the house was built of limestone from Bermuda (Charleston had been settled from Bermuda under William Sayle in the 1670s, and Bermudians retained close links with the city up to American independence).
